title: Isandro and the Sigil
premise: Isandro 'Bram' Kavanagh, a hedge-witch's runaway apprentice hiding in the Thornfell mountains, has spent three years erasing every trace of their old life—until the old gods wake and begin answering prayers with Isandro's stolen true name attached. Hunted by a king who is slowly being devoured by the sigil wearing his crown, and by the witch who trained them, Isandro must choose between vanishing forever or walking into the capital to unbind the monarch before the moon completes its thirteenth turn. In the end, Isandro severs the sigil at the cost of their own hidden name, trading invisibility for a self they finally claim as their own.
about_author: Gideon Eastwick is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent a decade mapping mountain passes before turning to fiction. They write stories about people the maps leave out.

chapters.title: The Thirteenth Moon Rises
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Smuggling salt through Thornfell, Isandro hears a prayer answered in their own erased voice—the first sign the old gods have woken. A dying pilgrim presses a wax-sealed token into their hands and whispers about a thing wearing the king's crown. The emotional beat is dread: the invisible life Isandro built is already burning.

chapters.title: What the Witch Kept
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. Forced back down the smuggler's roads to the hedge-witch Maren Kavanagh, who raised them, Isandro learns the truth: their stolen name was the binding-key to the royal sigil, sold by Maren years ago to buy Isandro's survival. Betrayal and grief collide; Maren offers to help them undo it, if Isandro can forgive her. The beat is bitter reconciliation.

chapters.title: A Crown of Hungry Light
chapters.summary: POV alternating between Isandro infiltrating the capital and King Aldric, lucid for minutes at a time inside his own devouring crown. Climax: during the moon's thirteenth turn, Isandro reaches the throne room and begins the unbinding while the sigil fights back through the court itself, wearing the faces of everyone Isandro has ever wronged. The beat is terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Name I Keep
chapters.summary: POV Isandro. The unbinding demands a name freely given; Isandro surrenders the stolen one, freeing King Aldric but leaving themselves unnamed in the gods' ledger—until they speak a new name, chosen, not taken. Aldric owes them a debt outside the law, and Maren waits on the mountain road. The beat is quiet triumph: survival was never free, but identity finally is.
